children: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth forcefully defended his leadership in the Iran war and military operations during his first Pentagon news conference in six months, dismissing the eight articles of impeachment introduced by Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., as "a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it.”

accuse Hegseth of waging war without congressional authority, carrying out extrajudicial killings tied to boat strikes in the Caribbean, and suppressing free speech by targeting Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz.
Incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., confirmed Democrats are a “hard yes” on impeaching the Defense Secretary.

Hegseth said the impeachment push "puts a target on the backs of American warriors by signaling that Congress will undermine their missions in real time," calling it “sabotage” rather than patriotism.
President Donald Trump backed his Pentagon chief on Truth Social, awarding him an "A PLUS, PLUS, PLUS" while labeling Massie "a TOTAL LOSER!"

The House is set to vote Tuesday on a procedural motion related to the impeachment resolution, which must be acted upon within two legislative days. If impeached, Hegseth would face a Senate trial requiring a two-thirds majority for conviction and removal—a threshold no U.S. Cabinet secretary has ever met.

title: Impeachment articles ‘a farce, and a stunt,’ says Pete Hegseth
